title: Latency Mosaic: p95/p99 Matrix & Regression Harness per Route/Model/Region
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Goal: Build a scalable p95/p99 telemetry pipeline and interactive 'Latency Mosaic' dashboard that shows percentile latency and tokens/sec across the three primary dimensions: route, model, region. The dashboard should enable fast drill-downs, historical baselining, and automated regression detection tied to the load testing harness (InferBench).

Background: We currently surface endpoint-level latencies but lack an efficient matrix view that highlights correlated regressions across route/model/region slices. As traffic grows and Dedicated deployments diversify by region, on-call and SREs need a single-pane view that points to problematic model variants or regions quickly. This ticket implements telemetry aggregation, visualization, and a regression-watcher integration that raises alerts when p95/p99 deviate beyond expected baselines during synthetic or production traffic.

Scope and Constraints:
- Produce rolling p95 and p99 for windows: 1m (low-latency), 5m (operational), 1h (baseline).
- Dimensions: route (API path), model (model id + quantization variant), region (cloud region or on-prem pool tag).
- Token throughput (tokens/sec) correlated per slice to spot batching/throughput regressions.
- Use approximation algorithm (t-digest) for percentiles to control memory vs accuracy. Target error <= 2% at p99 for typical distributions.
- Storage: 7 days of 1m rollups, 30 days of 5m rollups, 365 days of 1h rollups (rollup policy).
- Alerting: regression-watcher will compare current percentiles against N-day rolling baseline (default N=7) and open alerts when deviation > configured sigma or absolute ms threshold.

Telemetry pipeline design (high level):
1) Ingest: runtime emits per-request telemetry to kafka topic 'telemetry.latency.v2' including: route, model_id, model_variant, region, request_id, tokens_generated, latency_ms, timestamp, tokens_baseline_estimate.
2) Aggregator: stream processors (Flink/kstream) maintain per-slice t-digests that are flushed to a metrics store at 1m/5m/1h intervals. Use keyed aggregation by (route, model_variant, region).
3) Storage: time-series DB for visualizations (ClickHouse/Timescale) storing rollups and small t-digest blobs for re-aggregation. Separate table for tokens/sec time-series.
4) Dashboard: frontend renders a matrix (routes on Y, models on X) with region filter. Cells show color-coded p95/p99 split and tokens/sec sparkline. Clicking cell opens slice detail (distribution histogram, recent synthetic-run diffs, relevant PRs/rollouts).
5) Regression-watcher: scheduled job consumes rollups and compares percentiles to the baseline. On regression, create issue in Linear (auto-tag) + Slack pulse to #sre-latency and add runbook link.

Success criteria:
- Matrix dashboard loads first view within 2s for the top 50 routes and models (pagination for remaining rows/cols).
- p95/p99 rollups are available with <= 2% approximation error vs raw HDRHistogram for test datasets.
- Regression-watcher detects injected regressions from InferBench runs (controlled 20% latency bump) with true positive rate >= 95% and false positive rate < 2% over 14 day eval.
- On-call can triage a sliced regression to a specific model_variant or region within 10 minutes using dashboard and supporting links.

Non-goals:
- Full per-request raw storage (we do not store raw traces beyond short retention).
- Replacing tracing systems for root-cause profiling (we link to traces instead).
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry ingestion path creates 1m/5m/1h rollups keyed by route+model_variant+region
Frontend matrix shows combined p95/p99 color-coded view and tokens/sec sparkline per cell
t-digest implementation validated against HDRHistogram on synthetic datasets (error <= 2%)
Regression-watcher issues Linear tickets and posts Slack alerts when percentile deviations cross configured thresholds
Load-test integration: InferBench can push synthetic runs and the system flags injected regressions in a mirrored test workspace
Documentation: Confluence runbook + query snippets + retention policy published
updates: 2025-02-14 — Created ticket. Initial scoping and propose t-digest for approx percentiles. Assigned to Carlos.

2025-02-18 — Spike: implemented prototype aggregator in KStream. Verified per-slice t-digest memory at scale (~200k slices uses ~1.8GB across cluster). Next: storage schema for compact t-digests in ClickHouse.

2025-02-21 — Design review with SRE/Observability: settled on 1m/5m/1h rollups and 7/30/365 retention plan. Decided to limit cardinality by enforcing model_variant canonicalization and route grouping for SDK-internal noisy paths.
2025-02-24 — PR opened: telemetry producer changes (runtime) to include tokens_generated and model_variant. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1432 — awaiting infra review.
2025-02-26 — Dashboard mockups reviewed by PM and Design. Feedback: add stacked p95/p99 toggle and ensure colorblind-friendly palette. Filed small design follow-up DES-214 for palette tokens.
2025-02-28 — Regression detection prototype passed basic inferbench injection tests (single-model 30% latency spike). Working on lowering FP by adding minimum sample threshold per slice.
2025-03-01 — Blocker identified: some low-traffic slices have insufficient samples at 1m window — adding adaptive aggregation (fallback to 5m) and sampling guidance for InferBench synthetic runs.
notes: Cardinality control: we will limit model_variant label set by normalizing quantization labels and collapsing dev feature flags into 'experimental' bucket.
Consider adding a streaming anomaly detector if regression-watcher false positives are high; defer to follow-up ticket.
SRE requested canary gating: start with a single region and top-20 routes to validate before org-wide rollout.
Estimated infra cost: +0.4 vCPU/node for stream processors at current traffic; estimation in cost doc.
